data.title: Genmab Says Ovarian Cancer Drug Met Two Endpoints in Phase 3 Trial
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Genmab's ovarian cancer treatment met both its primary endpoint and a key secondary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial.

The company said Friday that Rina-S, or rinatabart sesutecan, significantly reduced the risk of disease progression in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, meeting a primary endpoint of progression-free survival.

The drug also met a key secondary endpoint of significantly improving overall survival among patients in the study.

Shares gained 6.8% on the news to $42.73 as of midday Friday. The stock is up 39% this year.

"These results advance our ambition to become a leader in gynecologic oncology and reflect our commitment to improving the lives of patients with high unmet medical needs," Chief Executive Officer Jan van de Winkel said.

The company said it plans to engage with global regulatory authorities to discuss potential next steps.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: American Express To Cut 5% Of Global Workforce; Raises 2026 EPS Outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • American Express posted adjusted EPS of $4.68, beating expectations of $4.49, while revenue of $20.06 billion came in just below the $20.12 billion estimate, according to Fiscal AI.
  • Provisions for credit losses fell to $1.0 billion from $1.3 billion a year earlier.
  • Net interest income rose 10% year over year to $4.94 billion, supported by growth in cardmember balances.

American Express Company (AXP) shares drew investor attention on Friday after the company reported third-quarter results and raised its full-year 2026 earnings per share (EPS) outlook while maintaining its revenue growth forecast.

On the Q3 earnings call, CEO Stephen Squeri said American Express recorded a $336 million restructuring charge and plans to eliminate approximately 5% of its global workforce as it seeks to improve organizational efficiency and agility.

AXP shares traded 3.5% lower at the time of writing.

Earnings And Guidance

American Express reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $4.68, beating consensus forecast of $4.49, while revenue of $20.06 billion came in below the $20.12 billion estimate, according to estimates compiled by Fiscal AI.

Net income rose 28% year over year to $3.71 billion, while diluted EPS increased 31% to $5.42 from $4.14. Adjusted EPS excludes the gain from the sale of the company’s equity interest in Global Business Travel Group (GBTG), net of the portion used to fund restructuring. The sale generated a $982 million pretax gain, while the restructuring charge was $336 million pretax.

Net interest income(NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 10% year-over-year to $4.94 billion, supported by growth in cardmember balances.

“Our business momentum continues, with strength in billings, new acquisitions and Card Member retention, and excellent credit quality,” CEO Stephen Squeri said.

Spending, Credit And Margins

According to management’s earnings-call commentary, billed business increased 8% to $454 billion, with travel and entertainment spending up 10%, airline spending up 13% and restaurant spending up 9%.

However the company reported consolidated provisions for credit losses of $1.0 billion, down from $1.3 billion a year earlier, reflecting a reserve release compared with a reserve build in the prior-year quarter, partially offset by higher net write-offs.

CFO Christophe Le Caillec said return on equity had risen from an average of 25%–28% about a decade ago to approximately 35% more recently. He also said the company expects variable customer engagement expense growth to moderate significantly in Q4 as it laps the prior-year U.S. Platinum Card refresh.

2026 Outlook

American Express maintained its full-year revenue growth forecast of 10% and raised reported EPS guidance to $18.30–$18.60, equivalent to 19%–21% growth. Adjusted EPS guidance rose to $17.60–$17.90, equivalent to 14%–16% growth.

Separately, Squeri said costs associated with remediation related to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) matter were not anticipated to affect 2027 guidance.

How Retail Views AXP 

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ a day ago, amid ‘high’ message volumes. AXP was also among the platform’s trending tickers at the time of writing.

AXP shares have dropped over 17% year-to-date.

data.title: AT&T, T-Mobile tighten AI guardrails as autonomous networks remain years away
data.description:
By Mehnaz Yasmin and Harshita Mary Varghese

Telecom giants AT&T and T-Mobile are investing to safeguard customer data and network infrastructure from new cybersecurity threats as AI integration ramps up, though fully autonomous networks remain years away, company executives told Reuters.

As AI agents automate workflows and data analysis, with declining human intervention, cybersecurity concerns are growing across industries over access to sensitive information and connected software.

For telecom operators, which manage vast amounts of customer data and critical communications infrastructure, vulnerabilities in AI systems or third-party software could extend from data breaches to network disruptions.

"Yes, we are increasing our investments in how we monitor and react," T-Mobile's Chief Technology Officer John Saw told the Reuters Global Markets Forum. The company simultaneously works with vendors to ensure security holes are closed as soon as possible, he added.

The Bellevue, Washington-based wireless carrier has suffered several data breaches, including incidents in 2021 and 2023, cumulatively impacting over 100 million customer accounts. It has agreed to various settlements with consumers and the Federal Communications Commission involving cybersecurity penalties and investments.

AT&T, meanwhile, warned that third-party software providers and AI agents pose cybersecurity risks that extend beyond operators' own networks.

"There (are) industry problems, not things that AT&T can solve by itself," CTO Jeremy Legg said, questioning if the open-source community followed comparable security standards.

The Texas-based company has deployed AI governance controls such as encryption, multi-factor authentication and human oversight of data access. It is also working to verify whether third-party AI agents seeking access to customer accounts are acting on behalf of legitimate customers, the company said.

AI has automated aspects of network management for telecom operators, but handing over entire networks to AI-driven autonomous systems is still "years away," Legg said, as human intervention is still required to solve complex network problems.

For instance, AT&T has automated some tasks such as analyzing trouble tickets to identify potential fixes and, in some cases, automatically implementing repairs. T-Mobile, meanwhile, uses AI to automatically adjust cell-site antennas when nearby sites go down to compensate for coverage gaps.

During Winter Storm Fern in January, T-Mobile's self-organizing network, or SON, restored coverage to about 66% of customers within an hour and 90% within eight hours, with most customers regaining service before power was restored, Saw said.

data.title: Starlink Is Years Away From Competing With AT&T and Verizon, Citi Says — But It Might Move Faster — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

Americans might have a fourth national telecom provider to complain about. SpaceX is coming, but how soon could it launch mobile service?

Citi analyst Michael Rollins sees it happening no earlier than 2029 and more likely 2030 to 2032.

That might be too conservative, but there are a few reasons for Rollins' timeline. For starters, SpaceX likely needs more wireless spectrum — essentially the pipes that carry wireless data. It has amassed about 80 megahertz of spectrum. T-Mobile US has about 400 megahertz.

SpaceX is likely to build its own ground-based network infrastructure, added Rollins in a Friday report.

The hardware alone would cost $20 billion. SpaceX would need to spend another $20 billion on more wireless spectrum. That's in addition to the ongoing spending on SpaceX's existing connectivity business. All told, additional spending on wireless communications could easily top $100 billion by 2031, he says.

It all takes time, but SpaceX could shortcut the process by just buying an existing player, Rollins says. It would also be a more capital-efficient way to launch service. Wireless telecoms trade at a discount to their assets.

For AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, the timing matters: A faster launch would give them less time to prepare for a new national competitor.

Musk's other ventures offer an example of how quickly his companies can move. What was then xAI brought its Colossus data center in Memphis online in 122 days. But Musk's ambitious deadlines haven't always held up.

He predicted one million robo-taxis on the road by 2020 and humans on Mars by 2025. Investors are still waiting. He's also predicted 20 million Tesla vehicle sales by 2030. (Tesla is expected to sell fewer than 2 million cars in 2026.)

SpaceX stock was up 1.7% in early trading after Bloomberg reported that SpaceX wanted 80,000 cell sites.

That sent shares of cell tower companies such as Crown Castle higher on Friday. Crown and its peers are like the apartment buildings of the telecom world. Wireless companies move in with their equipment. EchoStar stock was up 2%. Its spectrum portfolio looks more valuable. (It also owns SpaceX stock.) Wireless telecom stocks, including T-Mobile, fell between 2% and 5%.

SpaceX will eventually merge its satellite communications with ground-based infrastructure to provide service. SpaceX has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in low-Earth orbit.

Starlink is SpaceX's space-based broadband business that ended the third quarter with 13.6 million subscribers in 174 countries. Starlink's third-quarter sales and Ebitda were $5.2 billion and $3.5 billion, respectively.

data.title: GA-ASI Partnering With Spirit Defense For FQ-42 CCA Production
data.description:
SAN DIEGO, Oct 24, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), the world leader in Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), today is announcing our partnership with Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, to support airframe production of the new FQ-42 Vengeance Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA). In June, GA-ASI won a contract from the U.S. Air Force (USAF) to produce FQ-42. Spirit Defense's role as a fuselage design-build partner brings together the company's engineering and advanced manufacturing capabilities to support the program from design through production.

GA-ASI has been the sole manufacturer of its line of UAS - which includes MQ-9A Reaper, MQ-1C Gray Eagle, MQ-20 Avenger, and MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian - since the company's inception in 1992. For the FQ-42 program, partnering with Spirit Defense is a strength multiplier for the company and the nation, offering manufacturing capacity and industrial depth to scale CCA production faster, while strengthening production resilience, and reducing the risk of single points of failure.

"We're excited to be working with Spirit Defense," said GA-ASI President David R. Alexander. "We've established our proven design, development, and manufacturing capability for the FQ-42. With Spirit Defense we add capacity, which is exactly the kind of production resilience our U.S. Air Force customer is looking for with its CCA ramp-up. This kind of partnership represents the scalable industrial base the Air Force and the U.S. Department of War are looking for from industry."

"We're proud to bring deep manufacturing expertise and proven capabilities to this important program," said Keith Schrader, president and CEO of Spirit Defense. "Our team understands the responsibility that comes with supporting critical national defense programs, and we're ready to deliver for our customer and the warfighter."

FQ-42 is a purpose-built, uncrewed fighter, developed with USAF as part of ongoing investment in next-generation semi-autonomous combat aircraft. The jet's modular design enables rapid integration of mission systems and mission autonomy software. GA-ASI's software architecture, demonstrated through live flight tests on multiple airframes, provides the foundation for human-machine teaming in complex combat scenarios.

Potential CCA manufacturing partnerships don't end here. Around the world, GA-ASI is in discussions with numerous international militaries interested in our Gambit Series of modular CCAs. The Gambit Series is a family of uncrewed combat jets, derived from our work on FQ-42, XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station, and MQ-20 Avenger, and optimized for roles such as electronic warfare, suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), Destruction of Enemy Air Defenses (DEAD) and stand-off precision strike, making it a versatile option for evolving security needs.

Nations interested in procuring aircraft from the Gambit Series also have an opportunity to insert indigenous manufacturing into those programs, as well as integration of their own sensors, weapons and other combat technologies.

About Spirit Defense

Spirit Defense, a Boeing Company, is an independent supplier to the defense industry. Headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, the company provides engineering, design-build, manufacturing, and lifecycle support for defense programs. Leveraging more than a century of aircraft design and manufacturing experience, Spirit Defense helps customers move innovative concepts from development to production through rapid prototyping, scalable manufacturing, and proven aerospace expertise.

About GA-ASI

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc., is the world's foremost builder of Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS). Logging more than 9 million flight hours, the Predator line of UAS has flown for over 30 years and includes MQ-9A Reaper, MQ-1C Gray Eagle, MQ-20 Avenger, MQ-9B SkyGuardian/SeaGuardian, XQ-67A, and FQ-42 Vengeance. The company is dedicated to providing long-endurance, multi-mission solutions that deliver persistent situational awareness and rapid strike.

data.title: Tradr Announces Liquidation of SKHA and SKHN
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tradr ETFs, a provider of ETFs designed for sophisticated investors and professional traders, today announced that a plan of liquidation has been approved for the following funds:

Tradr 2X Long SK hynix Daily ETF (Cboe: SKHA)

Tradr 2X Short SK hynix Daily ETF (Cboe: SKHN)

Each Fund will allow creation and redemption of units through November 5, 2026, which will be the last day of trading on the Cboe BZX Exchange. On or about November 12, 2026, each Fund will cease operations, liquidate assets and prepare to distribute proceeds to shareholders of record.

For detailed information on Tradr ETFs and the significant risks involved with leveraged ETFs, please visit www.tradretfs.com.

About Tradr ETFs

Tradr ETFs are designed for sophisticated investors and professional traders who are looking to express high conviction investment views. The strategies include leveraged and inverse ETFs that seek short or long exposure to actively traded stocks and ETFs.

IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION

Tradr ETFs are for sophisticated investors and professional traders with high conviction views and are very different from most other ETFs. The Funds are intended to be used as short-term trading vehicles and pursue leveraged investment objectives, which means they are riskier than alternatives that do not use leverage because the Funds magnify the performance of their underlying security. The volatility of the underlying security may affect a Fund's return as much as, or more than, the return of the underlying security.

Investors in the fund should: (a) understand the risks associated with the use of leverage; (b) understand the consequences of seeking inverse and leveraged investment results; (c) for short ETFs, understand the risk of shorting; (d) intend to actively monitor and manage their investment. Fund performance will likely be significantly different than the benchmark over periods longer than the specified reset period and the performance may trend in the opposite direction than its benchmark over periods other than that period.

Leverage increases the risk of a total loss of an investor's investment, may increase the volatility of the Funds, and may magnify any differences between the performance of the Funds and their reference security. The Funds seek leveraged investment results for a specific period (daily, monthly or quarterly). The exact exposure of an investment in the Fund intra-period will depend upon the movement of the reference security from the end of the prior period until the time of investment by the investor.

The Fund will not attempt to position its portfolio to ensure it does not gain or lose more than a maximum percentage of its net asset value on a given trading day. As a consequence, investors in a Fund that seeks two times daily performance would lose all of their money if the Fund's underlying security moves more than 50% in a direction adverse to the Fund on a given trading day.

ETFs involve risk including possible loss of the full principal value. There is no assurance that the Fund will achieve its investment objective. Principal risks and other important risks may be found in the prospectus. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

ETF shares are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemed from the ETF. There can be no guarantee that an active trading market for ETF shares will develop or be maintained, or that their listing will continue or remain unchanged. Buying or selling ETF shares on an exchange may require the payment of brokerage commissions and frequent trading may incur brokerage costs that detract significantly from investment returns.

Investors should carefully consider the investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses of the Funds. This and other important information about the Fund is contained in the Prospectus, which can be obtained by visiting www.tradretfs.com. The Prospectus should be read carefully before investing.
